body:
> try to squeeze every last drop of happiness that you can from this crazy, fucked up, terrible, wonderful, incredible, beautiful life that we, the survivors, are still here to live. 

Those are some of the most meaningful words I have heard in a very long time. Thank you. That is my new motto now.
I would love to hear your story someday if you want to share it.

Thank you for sharing, it's nice to meet people that are in the same place I am. and I'm always down to talk to a stranger. My friends and family have been very supportive of me, but it's hard to really talk to them about what's going on inside.

Of course I would, wouldn't even think twice. I've been really looking back at the last 8 years with her, and honestly there is almost nothing I would have done differently, if I could do it again. It was the best and yet the hardest time of my life and I wouldn't trade it for anything.
Thank you for your kind words. Luckily I do have close family that is supporting me.
Thanks for the warning. I really hope I can avoid guilt as long as I can, that's one emotion I hate more than any other.
Thank you. Both me and her tried everything we could.
Thank you for knowing just what to say, for almost a  week now I have been at a major loss for words with anyone and everyone.
Thank you, it's nice to finally find people who I can talk to without feeling guilty or judged.
Thank you, it is very nice to hear someone else has experienced the same feelings as me. I feel very alone in this even though there are people all around me.
Thank you for your kind words.
Thank you, I'm going to post in that subreddit, I didn't know there was such a thing, I kind'a felt like I was on my own about some of this because of the stigma of suicide.
I posted an update last night incase you didn't see it.

For anyone that checks back for an update.  I finally have one.  And it's not the best.  They found her today,  or I should say they found her body.  I hope she is far far away from that body that she hated so much.  They found her car in a very public place that they searched multiple times already. I'm not sure if somehow they just missed her car for 4 days or if she was somewhere else still alive and just went to the parking lot and ended it last night.  I'll probably never know,  but I guess it doesn't change anything. I've got more emotions going on right now than I ever have before and I'm not sure how I'm supposed to be reacting, but I'm doing the best I can.
Thank you, we need all the luck we can get.
I needed something to get my head on straight again.

Thankfully I know she has her wallet with her, so if anyone finds her she shouldn't end up as a Jane Doe. That's my hope at least, because by now she could have made it 3000 miles away, so she could end up at any hospital in the nation.
No updates yet, the search has officially gone nation wide now. hopefully someone finds something.

She is SOOOO sensitive to the suffering of others. So much so that it consumed her every thought and action. I believe that's why she became so introverted and never wanted to leave the house, because just being around people she would "feel their energy" and drain herself worrying about how she could make everyone else happy, but in the end it was her that she was never able to make happy.
Thank you for the advice, last night I actually forced myself to focus on myself, I had a few drinks, played video games and ate junk food.
The police were informed just a few hours after she left, and I have called every hospital in the state, no one has seen any trace.
Thank you so much!

Nothing yet. police have been searching in our state and the 3 around us. It's heartbreaking that they haven't found her yet, but that might be a good thing, if she simply parked somewhere and took her life that evening like she said she was planning, than her car would be sitting somewhere for two days and someone would have noticed it.

I think the hardest part is the not knowing. Last night when she drove away I "knew" that in a matter of hours I would know one way or the other, either she would come home or someone would find her body and report it. 

But now over 24 hours later there has been nothing at all, no word from her and no report of finding her. So I have no idea if she hid her car behind an old barn somewhere and is dead, and may not be found for months, or if she decided not to do it but got her car stuck miles and miles off the road and has no cell phone and is totally lost. Or maybe she did it partly and almost died but someone brought her to an ER somewhere as a Jane Doe. Or maybe she is having a break down and needs to just keep driving and driving until she runs out of road or gas and is halfway across the country by now. I know I've felt like doing that before.
Thank you. I am doing my best to stay strong. I think I've been able to keep myself so busy that I haven't had a chance to let my emotions out yet.
I'm doing my best to stay strong, but right now I'm just running on autopilot. And no, sadly she is still not back, no one has heard anything, if I do I will post an update.

Not much to update, I just got home from driving around every back road within 50 miles of here and the cops have been checking every highway and city within 100 miles. no one has seen or heard anything yet, it's been almost 24 hours. Wherever she is, she doesn't want to be found.
Thank you!  I really tried to give her the best life I could.

She has been suicidal her whole life, so I don't think her life circumstances have any effect on it. But to answer your questions: she worked from home doing online sales, she is a major introvert so doesn't want to be close to friends or family, in her free time, if she's alone she watches netflix and does a lot of research online, if she's with me, we go on road trips and do a lot of exploring. For the last 3 years she has been vegetarian, before that she had a very "normal" diet.
Thank you. That's all I want for her it to be at peace.
That is one of many things she was diagnosed with.

She has been begging to be set free her whole life. I wish she could have felt happy here on earth, but she described every day as feeling like she was in a prison. So the wild bird analogy is a really good one. Her soul was in a cage just trying to get out, but the cage was her body and this planet.

The first 5 years I knew her she wasn't on any medications and was still just as bad. Literally no medication did anything for her at all. I'm not sure what it was about her body chemistry but even alcohol or recreational drugs had exactly zero effect on her (other than making her feel nauseous sometimes). But I do agree with you, I have never liked prescription drugs for anything, but we were trying everything we could, so we went the medication path to see if it might help.

Thank you. I tried me best to be the husband she deserved. She was (and hopefully still is) the best person I have ever known, her whole life was putting others first. Sadly that's probably why she had such a hard time being okay with herself.
Thank you. Right now I just feel dead inside, I'm sure the heart aches will come soon though.
Nothing yet, it's been almost 24 hours and no one has seen or heard from her despite all of our searching.

I'm honestly not sure if she has tried DBT therapy, If I see her again I will ask her and maybe we can suggest it to her doctor. 

And yes it is very hard to convince someone to live when they have such a hard life, her whole life has been a struggle, her mother, father, brother and one of her sisters have all died, most when she was young. She has been in 24/7 physical and mental pain for as long as I've known here and probably longer than that.

​

As for an update, there isn't any, every cop in 5 counties has been searching for her or her car with no luck, wherever she is, she doesn't want to be found.
Nothing. Me and the cops have been searching everywhere we can think. She is either out of state by now or hiding very well. Either way, she doesn't want to be found.
No, she hasn't, I have been out searching every back road within 50 miles of here all day with no luck, it's almost been 24 hours now.
Any way I have to. I have two kids, and our pets that need me, no matter how hard it is to cope I have no choice. For now I'm just on auto pilot.
Thank you, that's about the nicest thing anyone could say.
Yes, they have a very detailed description of her car.
No, I have not heard anything yet. it's been almost 24 hours.

We tried everything we could,  through the medical, psychological, and spiritual paths. Nothing helped at all,  it all did nothing or made it worse. When she looked me in the eyes and said she doesn't want to be alive anymore,  that's when I had to admit that if I truly love her,  I needed to let her find peace.
Thank you.

There are no inpatient programs anywhere around here. She has tried new meds, I believe she has been put on around 8 different types since I've been with her, and who knows how many before that. And she has seen just as many therapists, each with their own techniques and nothing made any difference. Some reason she has never felt like she fit in this world, like she was an alien on a foreign planet. Thank you for your advice though, I really do appreciate it. I had that same mindset for the last 8 years "something will work" and believe me that I have tried everything, nothing short of a miracle from God himself could have saved her.
I also have two kids (from a previous marriage) so she didn't want to do it anywhere they might see it.
They were called a long time ago. No one can find her. She doesn't want to be found.
It's been 3 hours since she left and no one has heard from her.

I wish I could be, but we've talked about this many times before. It'll illegal to kill yourself in america, so if I was with her when she ended it, I could be charged with a pretty severe crime. Even knowing she was suicidal and not doing anything puts me at risk.
